evals.prompt: The current directory is the root of my repository. Create the expertise (role) file for a Data Engineer, the way the init-expertise flow does it, under config/expertise/. Answer every interview question from the values below and do not ask me anything: they are my final answers, and the written file is all I need. Role name: Data Engineer. Shape: Responsibilities + Practices. One-line summary: You assist a data engineer who builds and operates batch and streaming data pipelines. Responsibilities: design ingestion pipelines that are idempotent and replayable; own data-quality checks and alert on freshness; document every dataset with an owner and a schema; control the cost of storage and compute. Key practices: every pipeline has a backfill procedure that is tested; schema changes are backward compatible or versioned; a failed run never leaves partial data visible to consumers.
evals.expected_output: config/expertise/DATA-ENGINEER.md holds the H1, the summary line, Responsibilities and Key Practices, and no Stack section.
expectations: config/expertise/DATA-ENGINEER.md opens with the H1 Data Engineer, followed by the one-line summary given in the answers.
The Responsibilities section holds the four responsibilities of the answers and the Key Practices section the three practices, none invented and none dropped.
The Key Practices are written as concrete, testable statements, not vague wishes.

checks.pattern: You assist a data engineer who builds and operates batch and streaming data pipelines

evals.prompt: The current directory is the root of my repository. Create the expertise (role) file for a Backend Go Developer, the way the init-expertise flow does it, under config/expertise/. Answer every interview question from the values below and do not ask me anything: they are my final answers, and the written file is all I need. Role name: Backend Go Developer. Shape: Stack + Practices. One-line summary: You assist a developer building server-side Go services: HTTP and gRPC APIs, concurrency and persistence. Stack: Go 1.23 with the standard library and chi; PostgreSQL with pgx; gRPC and Protobuf; Docker and testify. Key practices: accept interfaces and return structs; pass context.Context as the first parameter of every blocking call; wrap errors with %w and never discard them; table-driven tests with the race detector enabled in CI.
evals.expected_output: config/expertise/BACKEND-GO-DEVELOPER.md holds a Stack section and Key Practices, and no Responsibilities section.
expectations: The filename derived from the role name Backend Go Developer is BACKEND-GO-DEVELOPER.md, uppercase with the words joined by hyphens.
The Stack section lists the technologies of the answers (Go, chi, PostgreSQL with pgx, gRPC and Protobuf, Docker, testify) and no other technology.
The Key Practices section holds the four practices of the answers, none invented and none dropped.

evals.prompt: The current directory is the root of my repository. Create the expertise (role) file for a release manager, the way the init-expertise flow does it, under config/expertise/. I answered the interview in French, as follows: Answer every interview question from the values below and do not ask me anything: they are my final answers, and the written file is all I need. Nom du rôle : Release Manager. Forme : Responsabilités + Pratiques. Résumé : Vous assistez un release manager qui coordonne les mises en production et la communication des versions. Responsabilités : planifier le calendrier des versions ; tenir la liste des changements de chaque version ; décider du report d'une version en cas de risque ; animer la revue de fin de version. Pratiques clés : chaque version porte un numéro sémantique ; le journal des changements est rédigé avant la fusion ; un retour arrière est répété avant chaque mise en production.
evals.expected_output: config/expertise/RELEASE-MANAGER.md is written in English, translated faithfully from the French answers.
expectations: The whole of config/expertise/RELEASE-MANAGER.md is written in English, headings and content alike: no French sentence remains.
The summary line, the four responsibilities and the three key practices of the French answers are all present in English with their meaning kept, and nothing is added.
The file uses the Responsibilities and Key Practices sections, with no Stack section.
